evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Calvin: 'I'll just run, run through some questions with you and I'll be able to get you that estimate at the end. Does that work?' — Framing present but rushed past without strong time-box or 'dependable quote' promise language; customer says yes but it's a soft yes, not to a clear 10–15 minute commitment.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Calvin asks 'And anything at the moment that you're particularly concerned about. That I could kind of address before jumping in.' — Phrased as a soft open-ended check rather than the structured 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns' version, and it comes after the customer has already started volunteering concerns (not before probing). This is asked during the discovery flow, not as a dedicated agenda-setting moment.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises concern about furniture breakage (bed breakdown needed). Calvin responds: 'Yeah, we do that, we do disassemble and reassembly that's part of our hourly rate. So, yeah, we can definitely help with that.' Then customer says 'Oh, okay. Okay, perfect. That was the main thing.' Calvin does not follow up with 'tell me more about that' or dig deeper into what else might be at risk or what specific pieces need breakdown — he takes the 'perfect' as done and moves on.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No reflection offered. Calvin hears the concern and answers it directly but never summarizes back: 'So what I'm hearing is that you need bed disassembly and reassembly, and you want to make sure nothing gets broken this time. Did I get that right?'
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Covered: property type (home), destination access (driveway/street), elevator proximity, approximate contents (1-bedroom furniture inventory). Not clearly covered: floor/stories of either location, exact number of rooms, walking distance from truck to unit, special considerations beyond disassembly. Partial, not full.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not offered. No mention of 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Not asked. No mention of typical box count or overflow check.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Calvin: 'I would give you a budget between $826 and $1,023 which would be three and a half to four and a half hours of move time. The main thing that adds the most time for us is loose miscellaneous items that don't get box like Clos and pictures, or most efficient with big furniture impact boxes.' Personalized to the customer's 30–40 minute drive, elevator access, and disassembly/reassembly of the bed frame. Full anchor and personalization present.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Calvin discloses trip fee ($105) upfront, mentions $615 minimum (2.5 hours), 15-minute increments, hourly rate ($204), no taxes or credit card fees, insurance and pads included. He also frames it as 'the hourly rate...takes effect once they actually get on site' and 'you just pay for the time that was actually used that day.' Strong fee transparency and rate framing. Full.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked. After the estimate, customer asks clarifying questions about payment timing and deposit; Calvin answers those, then customer asks about weekend vs. weekday pricing; Calvin pivots into rate comparison. The 'does that feel fair' or equivalent check-in is never delivered.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Not mentioned. No On-Time Guarantee or discount-if-late framing offered.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Not mentioned. No No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000, no deductible, no fine print) delivered.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Not applicable — neither promise was delivered, so nothing to close the loop on.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Call ends with 'Sounds good. You have a great day and a great weekend.' No version of 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or genuine final concerns check.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. No 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' before the close.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never. Calvin never says 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any recognizable booking ask. Instead, he pivots to rate comparison, mentions the arrival window and email confirmation, and the customer volunteers 'Yeah. Yeah, I let's go ahead and put it on the calendar' — but Calvin never explicitly asked for the business.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Not mentioned. No rate-lock language or 'your quote is good for X days' framing.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Confirmed: date (November 21st), arrival window (8:30–9:00 AM), phone number (not explicitly confirmed, though email was provided). Missing: customer's phone number confirmed back, full destination address re-confirmed in the booking, crew size (2 movers confirmed in estimate but not in final booking summary), and crucially, no notes left for the crew about the disassembly/reassembly concern or any of the customer's stated worries.

top_strength: Calvin gathered comprehensive inventory details early and personalized the estimate precisely to the customer's specific move profile (drive time, elevator access, disassembly needs), resulting in a credible and detailed pricing range.
coaching_note: You must deliver the Two Promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) before closing, and never skip the explicit ask for the business — the customer's 'let's go ahead' was them filling in a gap you left, not you closing the sale.
